parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of the domain module holds together. Orders, order lines, status flow, products, stock allocation and the repository ports all belong to one ordering and stock concern, and nothing reaches persistence around the ports: StockAllocationService only uses ProductRepository.

The problem is the insufficient-stock rule, which exists in two places. Product.reserve checks `quantity > this.available` and throws DomainError("INSUFFICIENT_STOCK", "Insufficient stock for product ${id}: requested ..., available ...").

StockAllocationService.reserve writes out the same comparison against product.availableQuantity and throws the same error code with the same message template. It does not call a shared definition. The pre-check exists so that no line is reserved unless all of them can be, but it is still a second copy of the invariant and its error text. The two can drift apart; Product could instead expose something like canReserve().

A smaller point: assertOrderStatus in order-status.ts uses the error message "Query parameter 'status' must be a valid order status". That message is about the HTTP request, not the domain. It is a boundary leak but not serious enough to fail the unit by itself.

violations.message: StockAllocationService.reserve re-implements Product.reserve's insufficient-stock rule. It repeats the `quantity > available` comparison, the INSUFFICIENT_STOCK code and the message template instead of using one shared definition on Product (for example, a canReserve query).
